name: Coordinate Interval Comparison
statement: For every nonempty convex-realizable class $C$ and coordinate $i$, $W_i(C)\ge\tau(C)^{-2}$, with $0^{-2}=+\infty$. More precisely, for every $1<r<1/\tau(C)$ one cone realization and one positive center per concept support every individual coordinate interval with magnitude endpoints $z_i^c/r$ and $rz_i^c$ while all other magnitudes remain fixed.
proof: Choose coefficients and witness magnitudes with unfavorable-to-favorable ratio below $1/r$. Changing one magnitude by a factor in $[1/r,r]$ multiplies any comparison ratio by at most $r$, whether that term lies in the numerator, denominator, or neither. Every resulting ratio stays below one, and the endpoint magnitude ratio is $r^2$. Let $r$ approach $1/\tau(C)$.
comments: The intervals vary one coordinate at a time; no simultaneous box is claimed, and the infimum defining $\tau$ need not be attained.
